rows.finding: Eight full cases establish taking up incense as compiler-narrated ritual action before source-specific speech, dedication, question, or verdict; it remains distinct from burning.
Nine cases support the room/institution and metonymic resident-abbot senses; movement into the room and 方丈和尚 syntax keep the referents distinct.
Nine cases ground raising the teaching-seat whisk as answer, demonstration, and question; narrated gesture and direct appraisal are correctly separated without universal decoding.
Seven cases support one's own household treasure through possession and own-versus-imported contrast; the gloss avoids literal money or a concealed jewel.
Six attributed cases support bright and numinous while explicit Xuansha and later criticisms prevent identifying it with an enduring true self.
Fifteen cases justify the Caodong Five Ranks versus ordinary five-position senses; questions, compiler-introduced schemes, lay inquiry, and non-Caodong classifications are correctly owned.
Thirteen full cases consistently treat bowing/prostration as narrated ritual action before or after exchanges; no inward state is inferred from the gesture alone.
Five cases accurately represent Bai Juyi as poet-official and case figure; three Bird's-Nest witnesses are explicitly treated as parallel recensions, not independent events.
Eight cases establish taking up the staff as visible presiding action used to open, answer, punctuate, strike, or scatter; compiler wording remains distinct from following speech.
Eight cases ground the inaugural teaching-hall assembly and distinguish invitations/requested action from the discourse delivered there.
